cards.label: Last day to register to vote
Last day to request an absentee ballot

faq.a: Election Day is November 3, 2026. Polling locations are open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.. Anyone in line when the polls close is allowed to stay and vote. Individuals arriving after the polling place has closed will not be allowed to vote.

faq.q: How do I vote early (absentee ballot)?
faq.a: [Request a Missouri absentee ballot here.](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/ElectionGoVoteMissouri/AbsenteeBallotRequestForm.pdf) Voters in Missouri must provide a [reason](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/howtovote) for needing an absentee ballot. All absentee ballot requests must be received by the election authority no later than 5:00 p.m. on **October 21, 2026**. Voters can vote by absentee in the office of the local election authority until 5:00 p.m. the night before the election.
If you are registered to vote, find your polling place [here](https://voteroutreach.sos.mo.gov/portal/). You can only vote at your assigned polling place.

faq.q: What should I bring to the polls?
What if I moved since the last time I voted?
faq.a:
If you move or change your name, you’ll need to [update your registration to vote.](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/register)

If you moved to a different address within the same county, you can change your registration address on Election Day at your new polling place. Contact your local election official with address changes before Election Day to find your new polling place.

If you moved to Missouri after the deadline to register for a presidential election, you are entitled to register and vote only a presidential and vice presidential ballot in your new jurisdiction.

faq.q: Are there accessibility accommodations at my polling place?
faq.a: Every polling place must have an accessible voting system, including audiovisual accessibility. Accessible systems include an audio ballot to make selections or the ability to enlarge text. [View approved voting systems.](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/qualsystems)

faq.q: What's on my ballot and where do the candidates stand on issues I care about?
faq.a: See a [personalized ballot](https://www.vote411.org/ballot) for your voting location.

faq.q: If I have additional questions about voting, where should I go?
faq.a: There are plenty of resources to help you relay your voice this Election Day. Check out [Missouri’s official voting home page](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/govotemissouri) or find more digestible information from [Vote411](https://www.vote411.org/) or [The League of Women Voters](https://www.lwv.org/).
